boxes.head: Gaya
boxes.question: What is this mysterious kingdom?
boxes.about: A cone helm, a surrender, a name Bidam will later use. The country is shown before it is explained.

boxes.head: Gwansan
boxes.question: Why does Baekje call it a betrayal?
boxes.about: An old wound named before the battle is told.

boxes.head: The cone helm
boxes.question: Who is the unnamed Gaya prince?
boxes.about: A cone helm at Gwansan. The book will not say who until Muryuk.

boxes.head: Yongsu
boxes.question: Who is the boy who talks to the dark?
boxes.about: The identity box stays shut.

boxes.head: Ghost Bridge
boxes.question: Who dressed the stones in one night?
boxes.about: Servants say goblins. Yongsu answers.

boxes.head: The peonies
boxes.question: Why do Taizong’s flowers have no scent?
boxes.about: The gift arrives the morning she is crowned.

boxes.head: Yushin-ah
boxes.question: Why may he never say her name again?
boxes.about: The last time he is allowed to say it.

boxes.head: The east star
boxes.question: Will Chunchu pick the vow back up?
boxes.about: He puts it down. He picks it up again.

boxes.head: The thumb
boxes.question: Why does Elder Satek keep his thumb down?
boxes.about: A tourney that decides nothing.

boxes.head: Gyebek’s word
boxes.question: Who did he give his word to?
boxes.about: The river does not say. Hwangsan spends it.

boxes.head: The burn
boxes.question: Where did Gyebek see Gesomun?
boxes.about: I saw Gesomun again.

boxes.head: Eye
boxes.question: Who is the junior who is always right?
boxes.about: A soldier who is right every time Yeon gives an order.

boxes.head: The coat
boxes.question: What is on Pumsuk’s coat?
boxes.about: Gotaso sees it. He said he would change it later.

boxes.head: The latch
boxes.question: Which room only opens from inside?
boxes.about: Yushin will kneel in rooms he would burn.

boxes.head: Hangyul
boxes.question: What does the kite cost?
boxes.about: The horse that carries him three times. The kite needs a life.

boxes.head: Yumjong
boxes.question: Why does he say Gaya out loud?
boxes.about: A door Bidam pretends not to see open.

boxes.head: Queen Heo
boxes.question: Whose blood will Bidam claim?
boxes.about: Suro plants the line without knowing.

boxes.head: The lamp
boxes.question: Why does the room come to Chunchu?
boxes.about: Wherever the room has to come to you.

boxes.head: Deer Rock
boxes.question: Who poured the brine this afternoon?
boxes.about: Mu’s sealed-box rite.

boxes.head: The pass
boxes.question: Who will hold Tanhyeon?
boxes.about: Sunchung begs from prison. In 660 nobody is there.

boxes.head: Nine omens
boxes.question: Does the country already know?
boxes.about: Toads in the pines.

boxes.head: Class 77
boxes.question: Who is the mended-sleeve boy?
boxes.about: Bidam should pick him.

boxes.head: Three choices
boxes.question: Which road will Silla take?
boxes.about: The envoy in Chang’an. Chunchu’s later embassy answers it.

boxes.head: The half sword
boxes.question: Who will come south with it?
boxes.about: Lady Ye plants it.

boxes.head: Traitor
boxes.question: Who does Gusesa mean?
boxes.about: He drops it at the Summit. The massacre pays it.

boxes.head: The screen
boxes.question: Who saw Maehwa?
boxes.about: A cheap screen. Gumil already knows when he gets home.

boxes.head: Suulbu
boxes.question: What does he keep the house for?
boxes.about: I’ll keep the house. Bihyung spends what Jinhung plants.

boxes.head: The fox
boxes.question: Who built the bridge?
boxes.about: The bridge throws the fox off its own stones.

boxes.head: The locked door
boxes.question: How does she get out?
boxes.about: Heaven picks the house-apart. She goes out through the drain.

boxes.question: When does the count end?
boxes.about: It starts in the yard. It ends when the head comes back.

prologue-samhan::Back When Tigers Smoked.title: Back When Tigers Smoked
prologue-samhan::Back When Tigers Smoked.want: None. A trailer before the book.
prologue-samhan::Back When Tigers Smoked.development: Myth images, the fall, three kingdoms, the faces to come.
prologue-samhan::Back When Tigers Smoked.aPlot: A trailer before the book: tigers, the fall, three kingdoms, the faces to come.

themes.label: Overture
themes.note: No one wants anything. Keep it as the cold open.

prologue-samhan::Back When Tigers Smoked.problem: An overture, not a story. No one wants anything and nothing turns.

samhan::Queen Sunduk.title: Queen Sunduk
samhan::Queen Sunduk.want: Sunduk wants to prove she can rule ("I wonder whether I can do it at all"). Right now the episode keeps passing her to other people.
samhan::Queen Sunduk.conflict: The court will not crown a woman.
samhan::Queen Sunduk.development: She reads the room. The kids play on the sand. A girl is missing.
samhan::Queen Sunduk.climax: The peonies have no scent. Taizong sent a joke.
samhan::Queen Sunduk.aPlot: Dukman takes a throne nobody wants a woman to hold.
samhan::Queen Sunduk.bPlot: Yushin says her name one last time and walks to the wall.

themes.label: A woman on the throne
themes.note: The joke is the test.

samhan::Queen Sunduk.problem: Six points of view take turns before Sunduk gets a scene of her own. The real climax, reading the peonies' missing scent, comes after the envoy montage, so it plays like an afterthought.

samhan::Harmony Council.title: Harmony Council
samhan::Harmony Council.want: Bidam, the newest Council member, wants to break the 3–3 tie for Dukman.
samhan::Harmony Council.conflict: The vote is 3–3. Chunchu is rejected.
samhan::Harmony Council.development: The flame turns blue. The Three Counts stall.
samhan::Harmony Council.climax: Bidam speaks. Yushin answers from the wall. The vote is 6–0.
samhan::Harmony Council.resolution: Dukman is queen. Bidam is the man who said yes.
samhan::Harmony Council.aPlot: Bidam breaks a 3–3 tie for Dukman.
samhan::Harmony Council.bPlot: Chunchu waits outside. His father taught him the room comes to you.

themes.label: Who gets to choose a king
themes.note: Bone is the measure, until it isn’t.

samhan::Harmony Council.problem: It's a prequel to an outcome we've already seen, and Suljong changes his vote off-page. The night-bridge flashback interrupts the vote. A stray "High Councillor" fragment and a closing summary ("They argue past midnight…") retell a vote we just watched.

samhan::Jade Gate Valley.title: Jade Gate Valley
samhan::Jade Gate Valley.want: Bidam and Alchun, two Hwarang of Class 51, want one clean war against a foreign enemy, and Class 77 wants to see the legends.
samhan::Jade Gate Valley.conflict: Silla wants a foreign war. The valley is empty.
samhan::Jade Gate Valley.development: The yard. A monk is a bead short. Two of Class 51 ride in.
samhan::Jade Gate Valley.climax: Five hundred men were hiding in the valley.
samhan::Jade Gate Valley.resolution: The war they wanted is not the war they get.
samhan::Jade Gate Valley.aPlot: Bidam and Alchun want one clean war against a foreign enemy.

themes.label: Class 51
themes.note: Two men, one yard, a country that will pick between them.

samhan::Jade Gate Valley.problem: The yard talks for a while before the drums; the bone-rank gossip and the rail banter are two warm-ups in a row.

samhan::Jinhung, the Cloud.title: Jinhung, the Cloud
samhan::Jinhung, the Cloud.want: Sumekbu wants the border, then the girl, then a lighter robe.
samhan::Jinhung, the Cloud.conflict: Great Gaya still stands. Baekje is coming.
samhan::Jinhung, the Cloud.development: Gaya surrenders. Guhae and his sons take up new jobs in Silla.
samhan::Jinhung, the Cloud.climax: A slave takes King Sung’s head at Gwansan.
samhan::Jinhung, the Cloud.resolution: Jinhung has too many stones and a robe that no longer fits.
samhan::Jinhung, the Cloud.aPlot: Sumekbu wants the border, then the girl, then a lighter robe.
samhan::Jinhung, the Cloud.bPlot: Suulbu keeps the house. A cone helm watches a king die.

themes.label: The soft year
themes.note: A king who won too much and wanted less.

samhan::Jinhung, the Cloud.problem: The girls-into-the-river joke still sits after the ditch; some readers will feel the whiplash. Suulbu’s hunger is planted, not spent (that’s Bihyung’s job).

samhan::Prince Euija.title: Prince Euija
samhan::Prince Euija.want: Euija, crown prince at last, wants one person the clans don't own.
samhan::Prince Euija.conflict: The eight clans already own his brothers.
samhan::Prince Euija.development: He dives with Gyebek. He gives him a name no clan picked.
samhan::Prince Euija.climax: Do you like the name, or me?
samhan::Prince Euija.resolution: Gyebek is his. The court still will not explain Gwansan.
samhan::Prince Euija.aPlot: Euija wants one person the clans do not own.
samhan::Prince Euija.bPlot: Gyebek dives nineteen times for a word he will not explain.

themes.label: A name no clan picked
themes.note: The first thing that is his.

samhan::Prince Euija.problem: Gyebek's "I gave my word" is never explained, so the dives have no stakes and no payoff. The episode ends on narration about Yung instead of a turn.

samhan::Eight Great Clans.title: Eight Great Clans
samhan::Eight Great Clans.want: None. The two elders spar but want nothing new.
samhan::Eight Great Clans.conflict: Satek against Yunbi, frozen by design.
samhan::Eight Great Clans.resolution: King Mu: learn their names. Nobody has settled four generations of anything.
samhan::Eight Great Clans.aPlot: Satek against Yunbi, frozen by design.
samhan::Eight Great Clans.bPlot: A tourney that decides nothing. A thumb stays down.

themes.label: Clan over country
themes.note: A diagram of how power sits still.

samhan::Eight Great Clans.problem: The tourney decides nothing ("nobody has settled four generations of anything"), and the rest is two diagrams of how power works. Elder Satek's thumb-down is a good mystery that never pays off.

samhan::Deer Rock.title: Deer Rock
samhan::Deer Rock.want: Satek Jijuk, a junior Satek nobody rates, wants the Premier's chair that Elder Yunbi has already bought.
samhan::Deer Rock.conflict: Yunbi's four bought houses, a paid monk, and King Mu's revived sealed-box rite (Samguk Yusa), which every house means to rig.
samhan::Deer Rock.development: The old Premier dies · three names · brine poured since this afternoon · the night on the wall.
samhan::Deer Rock.climax: Dawn: Yunbi’s fresh seal bleeds. Jijuk’s dry one stands.
samhan::Deer Rock.resolution: The bottom step, the bet, the chant. A junior nobody rates takes the chair.
samhan::Deer Rock.aPlot: Jijuk wants the Premier’s chair Yunbi has already bought.
samhan::Deer Rock.bPlot: Gyebek was not asked. A monk’s stamp, a rock that sweats.

themes.label: A rite everyone means to rig
themes.note: The rock still picks.

samhan::Deer Rock.problem: Jijuk is seen only from outside until the last scene. That is the design, but he has one real conversation.

samhan::Gunchogo, the 13th.title: Gunchogo, the 13th
samhan::Gunchogo, the 13th.development: Six lines of chant and narration.
samhan::Gunchogo, the 13th.aPlot: A chant on a wall. A sentence that will get a fortress burned.

themes.label: A country is a story
themes.note: Planted here. Euija will spend it.

samhan::Gunchogo, the 13th.problem: A placeholder that also gives away a future beat ("the sentence that gets Daeya burned").

samhan::Commander Yeon.title: Commander Yeon
samhan::Commander Yeon.want: Gesomun wants to hold the east and stay out of Pyongyang.
samhan::Commander Yeon.conflict: The traitor, the Mohe, and his father's summons.
samhan::Commander Yeon.resolution: The seal is pushed across the table. He will go.
samhan::Commander Yeon.aPlot: Gesomun wants to hold the east and stay out of Pyongyang.
samhan::Commander Yeon.bPlot: A traitor with no name. A boy in a doorway.

themes.label: Half
themes.note: The father’s measure becomes the son’s.

samhan::Commander Yeon.problem: Three vignettes that don't touch. The traitor's "I have no name" copies Gyebek and goes nowhere, and the flash-forward to Pyongyang uses up Gulgul's ending.

samhan::Five Tribes.title: Five Tribes
samhan::Five Tribes.want: Gesomun wants to get his pregnant wife to the old Pyongyang house before the Summit, at the pace of an ox.
samhan::Five Tribes.conflict: The road (singing ice, wall deserters, the breaking Amnok, a cracked axle) and a junior soldier, Eye, who is right every time Yeon gives an order.
samhan::Five Tribes.development: The cart · singing ice · shut doors · the five stones · the raft · the pine axle.
samhan::Five Tribes.resolution: Pyongyang from the ridge. The unasked name waits.
samhan::Five Tribes.aPlot: Gesomun wants his pregnant wife to the old house before the Summit, at the pace of an ox.
samhan::Five Tribes.bPlot: Eye is right every time Yeon gives an order.

themes.label: Whose are you?
themes.note: Five roofs. One question he will not answer.

samhan::Five Tribes.problem: The middle runs as a string of road stops, and the five-roof explanation leans on the wife to finish it.

samhan::High Summit.title: High Summit
samhan::High Summit.want: Gesomun wants the Summit to prepare for Taizong.
samhan::High Summit.conflict: Four commanders, Gusesa, and the king's "King for All" budget.
samhan::High Summit.climax: Gusesa drops the word traitor. The people cheer.
samhan::High Summit.resolution: You will have to keep it. A newborn, and a list.
samhan::High Summit.aPlot: Gesomun wants the Summit to prepare for Taizong.
samhan::High Summit.bPlot: Namseng is born while the room calls his father a traitor.

themes.label: King for All
themes.note: The budget that will bury him.

samhan::High Summit.problem: The argument is position papers read in turn, and nobody spends anything, so the walkout changes nothing. The Samsin birth is a separate story bolted on.

samhan::Gwanggeto, the Great King.title: Gwanggeto, the Great King
samhan::Gwanggeto, the Great King.aPlot: A stele and a question: why are they still here?

themes.label: The record on the stone
themes.note: A stub that belongs with Stele.

five-principles::Bupmin.title: Bupmin
five-principles::Bupmin.want: Bupmin wants the headband to mean something besides his father's name.
five-principles::Bupmin.conflict: The yard names him hwarang on day one and leaves him with no disciples. Yushin will not be his uncle on the dust.
five-principles::Bupmin.development: The Class 82 gate · the picking · the throat · Gotaso at the pine · gyuku.
five-principles::Bupmin.climax: The Five Precepts. Which will you break first?
five-principles::Bupmin.resolution: Three disciples. The wall into Sadaham.
five-principles::Bupmin.aPlot: Bupmin wants the headband to mean something besides his father’s name.
five-principles::Bupmin.bPlot: Yushin will not be his uncle on the dust.

themes.label: A borrowed name
themes.note: The headband is not yet his.

five-principles::Bupmin.problem: The want is now on the page, but the episode still hands off to Sadaham before Bupmin's band is more than three boys. The wall walk is a history lesson in the last act.

five-principles::Sadaham.title: Sadaham
five-principles::Sadaham.want: Sadaham wants to ride to war with Mugwan and keep their swear.
five-principles::Sadaham.conflict: The king wants captives. Sadaham swore with Mugwan.
five-principles::Sadaham.development: He begs for the prisoners. Then he stops eating.
five-principles::Sadaham.climax: Seven days. Who would you stop eating for?
five-principles::Sadaham.resolution: He cuts the ropes. Friendship is the principle he will not break.
five-principles::Sadaham.aPlot: Sadaham wants to ride to war with Mugwan and keep their swear.
five-principles::Sadaham.bPlot: Bupmin asks which principle you break first.

themes.label: Friendship
themes.note: The one principle he will starve for.

five-principles::Sadaham.problem: The best self-contained episode in the set. The frame is thin: Bupmin asks a question and isn't changed by the answer.

five-principles::Gotaso.title: Gotaso
five-principles::Gotaso.want: First Chunchu, who wants his daughter back. Then Gotaso, who wants Pumsuk.
five-principles::Gotaso.development: Abduction · the ford · gyuku · flowering trees.
five-principles::Gotaso.climax: Four children. There is something on your coat.
five-principles::Gotaso.resolution: She chooses Pumsuk out loud. The coat will wait.
five-principles::Gotaso.aPlot: Gotaso wants to pick her own life before someone picks it for her.
five-principles::Gotaso.bPlot: Chunchu wants his daughter back. Nineteen li.

themes.label: Picking her own life
themes.note: Having been carried home is why she chooses fast.

five-principles::Gotaso.problem: The protagonist switches halfway. The narrator slips into "I did not know, then…," which breaks the never-say-I rule. Her age jumps between 16 and fifteen.

five-principles::Pumsuk.title: Pumsuk
five-principles::Pumsuk.want: Nominally Pumsuk. In practice it's Sunduk and Yushin.
five-principles::Pumsuk.conflict: Chunchu's vow, then the Queen's duty.
five-principles::Pumsuk.development: Munhee objects · the vow · the couple leaves · lantern-sellers.
five-principles::Pumsuk.climax: The vow. A fortress as a dowry.
five-principles::Pumsuk.resolution: They ride west. The near-miss stays a near-miss.
five-principles::Pumsuk.aPlot: Chunchu hands him Daeya as a wedding gift. He is too green for it.
five-principles::Pumsuk.bPlot: Sunduk and Yushin miss each other in a lantern street.

themes.label: A vow that is a trap
themes.note: Kindness is not a want. The fortress is.

five-principles::Pumsuk.problem: Pumsuk has no scene alone and no want beyond being kind. The episode's climax belongs to two other people. Haesang and the "girl-child" flashback are digressions.

five-principles::Munhee.title: Munhee
five-principles::Munhee.want: Munhee wants Chunchu and the dream she bought.
five-principles::Munhee.conflict: Propriety, and her own brother staging a scandal.
five-principles::Munhee.development: Buying the dream · the torn coat · the closed months.
five-principles::Munhee.resolution: Bupmin is born. Let it just be a star. Chunchu puts the east star down.
five-principles::Munhee.aPlot: Munhee wants Chunchu and the dream she bought.
five-principles::Munhee.bPlot: Her brother stages a scandal so the country has to say yes.

themes.label: A scandal as a door
themes.note: She buys a dream and walks through fire for it.

five-principles::Munhee.problem: The pyre climax falls in the middle and is followed by a long, turnless "Closed Months." Two paragraphs ("He comes back the next day…", "On a later visit…") are pasted twice. The pregnancy that sets off the pyre is never planted.

five-principles::Academy.title: Academy
five-principles::Academy.want: Gesomun wants a third leg for the pot that doesn't own a farm.
five-principles::Academy.development: Spring gate · summer Daoist chair · autumn empty room · winter county schools.
five-principles::Academy.climax: Gusesa’s supper. The seal argument in the boys’ room.
five-principles::Academy.resolution: Enrolment as a campaign. No turn yet — the list is still being written.
five-principles::Academy.aPlot: Gesomun wants a third leg for the pot that does not own a farm.
five-principles::Academy.bPlot: Namseng is caught at Boduk’s lesson. The east room empties.

themes.label: Who the country teaches
themes.note: A pot with three legs. The monasteries have two.

five-principles::Academy.problem: Good plants (Bodeok, Gulgul never sitting with his back to a door) but no event and no turn. It's a scene about enrolment.

five-principles::Stele.title: Stele
five-principles::Stele.aPlot: A stone. Sons who think it is a big rock.

themes.label: A big rock
themes.note: The irony is Namseng’s later question.

five-principles::Dosuryu.title: Dosuryu
five-principles::Dosuryu.conflict: The king and Gusesa plotting in secret.
five-principles::Dosuryu.climax: The laugh stops. I’ll make a list too.
five-principles::Dosuryu.resolution: The guest list is a kill list. Summer will be bowing.
five-principles::Dosuryu.bPlot: The king and Gusesa plot in secret.

themes.label: A warning he will not take
themes.note: The friend who puts his boots on.

five-principles::Dosuryu.problem: A strong scene with a real turn, but it's half an episode. The summer of bowing that 24 summarizes ("All summer he has bowed") is exactly the middle this one is missing.

five-principles::King Euija.title: King Euija
five-principles::King Euija.want: Euija wants to own his country through stories.
five-principles::King Euija.conflict: Gyebek's refusal to lie, and Seongchung's conscience.
five-principles::King Euija.development: The fake dragon · the miracles list · the Rock · the maids.
five-principles::King Euija.climax: How fortunate the rock has such good taste.
five-principles::King Euija.resolution: Pung is sent away. The theatre has a price.
five-principles::King Euija.aPlot: Euija wants to own his country through stories.
five-principles::King Euija.bPlot: Gyebek will not lie. Seongchung still has a conscience.

themes.label: A country is a story
themes.note: He is the one licensed to say the book’s idea out loud.

five-principles::King Euija.problem: The Euija–Gyebek comic engine is great, but it repeats rather than escalates. "The sentence that kills him, nineteen years later" points at no particular sentence. The maid scene stalls the episode.

five-principles::Yunchung.title: Yunchung
five-principles::Yunchung.want: Euija wants a war abroad to win the court at home.
five-principles::Yunchung.development: Yunchung on the good cushion · the shipping writ.
five-principles::Yunchung.climax: A country is a story. Daeya by autumn.
five-principles::Yunchung.resolution: The war is decided. Gyebek’s saving-you is the cost.
five-principles::Yunchung.aPlot: Euija wants a war abroad to win the court at home.
five-principles::Yunchung.bPlot: The Assembly, and a rock that can be made to sweat.

themes.label: A country is a story
themes.note: He says it in a room that will die for it.

five-principles::Yunchung.problem: He decides in the first scene, and nobody seriously opposes him after that. The Assembly scenes are a meeting followed by a speech.

five-principles::Gwansan.title: Gwansan
five-principles::Gwansan.want: King Sung wants not to be Gaya next.
five-principles::Gwansan.conflict: Baekje sent gifts. Silla kept the Han flags.
five-principles::Gwansan.development: King Sung marches first. The ditch is already waiting.
five-principles::Gwansan.climax: A slave takes the head and walks it home.
five-principles::Gwansan.resolution: Baekje calls it a betrayal. Silla has the Han.
five-principles::Gwansan.aPlot: King Sung wants not to be Gaya next.
five-principles::Gwansan.bPlot: A cone helm watches. A slave walks home under a Silla cloud.

themes.label: I am Silla tonight
themes.note: Leave that line to Muryuk.

five-principles::Gwansan.problem: The grandmother frame still carries a lot of the march. The cone helm must stay unnamed.

iron-will::Gumil.title: Gumil
iron-will::Gumil.want: Unclear. Yushin wants counsel, Seohyeon wants water, and Gumil gets about four lines.
iron-will::Gumil.conflict: A True Bone boy rides into Gumil’s own yard.
iron-will::Gumil.development: The cavern. Maehwa walks the cheap screen. The feast starts without him.
iron-will::Gumil.climax: He is passed over in his own house.
iron-will::Gumil.aPlot: Gumil wants clothes for his wife, and a rank the True Bone boy just rode in on.
iron-will::Gumil.bPlot: Yushin wants counsel. Seohyeon wants water.

themes.label: Classism
themes.note: A True Bone boy rides in. The local man is furniture.

iron-will::Gumil.problem: Three episodes in one, and the title character barely appears. A pasted "chunchu: Th-the father of that child…" line from 14 sits in the middle of the Daeya section.

iron-will::Maehwa.title: Maehwa
iron-will::Maehwa.want: Maehwa wants to be the one in control, to ruin the boy a little.
iron-will::Maehwa.conflict: She reaches up. He is True Bone.
iron-will::Maehwa.development: He can’t sleep. She teaches him. They fall.
iron-will::Maehwa.climax: She loses control. He leaves without a word.
iron-will::Maehwa.aPlot: Maehwa wants to be the one in control, to ruin the boy a little.
iron-will::Maehwa.bPlot: Pumsuk keeps his self-control. Then he doesn’t.

themes.label: Hypergamy
themes.note: She reaches up. The reaching undoes her.

iron-will::Maehwa.problem: The turn (teacher becomes undone) works, but then six or so escalating positions repeat it without changing anything. "In love" isn't earned, and it never pays off: Maehwa disappears from the story.

iron-will::Siege of Daeya.title: Siege of Daeya
iron-will::Siege of Daeya.want: Gumil wants revenge; Gotaso wants her husband to face her.
iron-will::Siege of Daeya.development: The confession · three weeks · Mochuk’s question.
iron-will::Siege of Daeya.climax: Everyone is trash. The men march out and are cut down.
iron-will::Siege of Daeya.resolution: Grief in Surabol. Chunmyung’s knee. The coat is paid.
iron-will::Siege of Daeya.aPlot: Gumil wants revenge. The gate opens from the inside.
iron-will::Siege of Daeya.bPlot: Gotaso wants her husband to face her. Kangrim will ask the question.

themes.label: Classism, spent
themes.note: The local man opens the gate.

iron-will::Siege of Daeya.problem: The siege, the actual climax of the arc, is told in summary ("Three weeks later…"). Pumsuk's surrender bargain comes *after* the reaper's question, so the order is scrambled. Jukjuk appears from nowhere, and Maehwa's fate is skipped.

iron-will::Yeon’s Massacre.title: Yeon’s Massacre
iron-will::Yeon’s Massacre.conflict: The Summit, which plans to bury him.
iron-will::Yeon’s Massacre.climax: The speech. Bojang. You there — what is your name?
iron-will::Yeon’s Massacre.resolution: Tell them that too. The closed kingdom begins.
iron-will::Yeon’s Massacre.aPlot: Gesomun wants the country. The Summit planned to bury him.
iron-will::Yeon’s Massacre.bPlot: His wife’s promise. A king who will sit.

themes.label: The guest list was a kill list
themes.note: Every Summit line pays off.

iron-will::Yeon’s Massacre.problem: Every Summit line from 8 pays off, which is excellent. "You there… what is your name?" appears twice. The aftermath runs long.

iron-will::Chunchu & Yeon.title: Chunchu & Yeon
iron-will::Chunchu & Yeon.want: Chunchu wants Goguryeo's troops and to make it home within sixty days.
iron-will::Chunchu & Yeon.development: Sixty days · Hadong · the cell · turtle-and-rabbit.
iron-will::Chunchu & Yeon.climax: The letter. Yushin’s camp on the clock.
iron-will::Chunchu & Yeon.resolution: Released on the king’s word. The empty saddle is the image he keeps.
iron-will::Chunchu & Yeon.aPlot: Chunchu wants Goguryeo’s troops and to make it home in sixty days.
iron-will::Chunchu & Yeon.bPlot: Yeon’s price for the passes. A bleeding hand. A rabbit.

themes.label: King for All
themes.note: He will pick the star back up.

iron-will::Chunchu & Yeon.problem: Two escapes compete. The rabbit-trick letter is clever, then Yushin's army makes it irrelevant.

iron-will::Euija & Yeon.title: Euija & Yeon
iron-will::Euija & Yeon.want: Euija wants Goguryeo's troops against Silla.
iron-will::Euija & Yeon.conflict: Yeon's same single price, and a blade on the table.
iron-will::Euija & Yeon.resolution: No troops. A warning about the man who just left.
iron-will::Euija & Yeon.aPlot: Euija wants Goguryeo’s troops against Silla.
iron-will::Euija & Yeon.bPlot: The same single price, and a blade on the table.

themes.label: Politics is alchemy
themes.note: Two kings, one price.

iron-will::Euija & Yeon.problem: No result. Does Euija get troops? The episode never says, and ends on maids.

iron-will::Nangbi.title: Nangbi
iron-will::Nangbi.want: Yushin wants to turn a lost battle and earn his father's word.
iron-will::Nangbi.conflict: The Goguryeo wall, and his silent father.
iron-will::Nangbi.climax: Your helmet’s crooked. Hangyul is named.
iron-will::Nangbi.resolution: Then I’ll kill him before they stop. A horse for eighteen years.
iron-will::Nangbi.aPlot: Yushin wants to turn a lost battle and earn his father’s word.
iron-will::Nangbi.bPlot: Yeon Taejo reads the report three times.

themes.label: Duty
themes.note: Three times. The horse is the witness.

iron-will::Nangbi.problem: Four Samguk Sagi quotes retell the charge we've just seen, against the house rule.

iron-will::Yushin.title: Yushin
iron-will::Yushin.want: Sunduk wants peace, then wants the forty back. Yushin fetches the means.
iron-will::Yushin.conflict: Daeya's wound versus the road her father kept.
iron-will::Yushin.development: Euija panic · unrest · the cavern · life flashbacks.
iron-will::Yushin.climax: Forty. One river fort. The water is the turn.
iron-will::Yushin.aPlot: Sunduk wants peace, then wants the forty back.
iron-will::Yushin.bPlot: Yushin fetches the means from a bucket in the hill.

themes.label: Duty
themes.note: He stands. He does not sit in lotus.

iron-will::Yushin.problem: The battle half is still montage after the water.

iron-will::The Eastern Star.title: The Eastern Star
iron-will::The Eastern Star.want: Chunchu, Euija and Gesomun each want to be the "King for All."
iron-will::The Eastern Star.climax: Chunchu picks the star back up.
iron-will::The Eastern Star.resolution: A thematic coda. The scar is the hook.
iron-will::The Eastern Star.aPlot: Chunchu, Euija and Gesomun each want to be the King for All.
iron-will::The Eastern Star.bPlot: Gyebek’s scar. I saw Gesomun again.

themes.label: King for All
themes.note: Three vows, no event. The box is the scar.

iron-will::The Eastern Star.problem: A thematic triptych with no event. Gyebek's burn scar and "I saw Gesomun again" is a good mystery, buried in the middle.

epilogue::Four Dragons.title: Four Dragons
epilogue::Four Dragons.aPlot: Taizong hears a name he will mispronounce.

themes.label: Teaser
themes.note: A card, not an episode.

epilogue::Four Dragons.problem: A teaser card, not an episode.

seventh-invasion::Emperor.title: Emperor
seventh-invasion::Emperor.want: The Second Emperor wants to finish what the Sui couldn't and lead the conquest of Goguryeo himself.
seventh-invasion::Emperor.conflict: Almost none on the page. Wei Zheng dies, and Chu Suiliang's one objection is waved away.
seventh-invasion::Emperor.development: The name taboo · Wei Zheng’s deathbed · foreign reports · the muster.
seventh-invasion::Emperor.resolution: The war is his. The room will not say his name.
seventh-invasion::Emperor.aPlot: The Second Emperor wants to finish what the Sui could not.
seventh-invasion::Emperor.bPlot: There will be no one left to tell him no.

themes.label: No one left to tell you no
themes.note: Charm as a weapon.

seventh-invasion::Emperor.problem: This is five setups stitched together. The strongest idea is "there will be no one left to tell you no", and it never gets tested: nobody says no in a scene the emperor has to win. The Daoist and bell beat and the Silla envoy beat belong to other storylines, and Xue's mini-story sits in the coda.

seventh-invasion::Sima Yi.title: Sima Yi
seventh-invasion::Sima Yi.want: A young Goguryeo king wants a teacher in the West. Sima Yi wants a friend who will not ask him to hurry.
seventh-invasion::Sima Yi.conflict: Distance, Zhuge Liang's legend, a friendship a hill king cannot keep.
seventh-invasion::Sima Yi.development: A horse trader’s lie · the thousand-li ride · the empty camp stool.
seventh-invasion::Sima Yi.resolution: The cost lands on Dongcheon. The wait was the friendship.
seventh-invasion::Sima Yi.aPlot: A young Goguryeo king wants a teacher in the West.
seventh-invasion::Sima Yi.bPlot: Sima Yi wants a friend who will not ask him to hurry.

themes.label: Friendship
themes.note: Distance is the conflict.

seventh-invasion::Sima Yi.problem: Some of the waiting is still rumour rather than a scene.

seventh-invasion::Yodong.title: Yodong
seventh-invasion::Yodong.want: The Second Emperor wants to break the fortress that held off the Sui.
seventh-invasion::Yodong.conflict: Yodong's walls, the marsh, and Goguryeo's faith in its founder.
seventh-invasion::Yodong.development: The Blue Dragon walks the wall · the marsh · he carries earth.
seventh-invasion::Yodong.climax: The south wind, the fire, the fall.
seventh-invasion::Yodong.resolution: A list of other forts. History? I am the one writing it.
seventh-invasion::Yodong.aPlot: The Second Emperor wants the fortress that held off the Sui.
seventh-invasion::Yodong.bPlot: A bride offered to Jumong. Twelve days.

themes.label: I am writing it
themes.note: The showdown belongs at Ansi.

seventh-invasion::Yodong.problem: The set pieces are strong, but Goguryeo has no face. The bride offered to Jumong is the most human beat in the arc and gets two lines. The emperor's showdown with Yang Manchun happens here, which takes the payoff away from Ansi, and "The Rest of the Line" is a list.

seventh-invasion::Boiling River.title: Boiling River
seventh-invasion::Boiling River.want: King Dongcheon wants a third victory over Guanqiu Jian.
seventh-invasion::Boiling River.conflict: His own overconfidence and a Wei army.
seventh-invasion::Boiling River.development: Beginning: a summary. Middle: none. End: Hwando burns, and an officer dies in the king's place.
seventh-invasion::Boiling River.aPlot: Dongcheon wants a third victory. He does not look at the ground.

themes.label: The king who did not look at the ground
themes.note: A caution for Stallion Mountain.

seventh-invasion::Boiling River.problem: It's eight lines of summary. The officer who wears the royal robes, the one dramatic act, is narrated in a clause.

seventh-invasion::Stallion Mountain.title: Stallion Mountain
seventh-invasion::Stallion Mountain.want: Xue Rengui wants his hour. Sul Gedu wants the cap, the sash and the sword. Namseng wants to save his brother.
seventh-invasion::Stallion Mountain.conflict: The Goguryeo relief army. For Namseng, the emperor's offer.
seventh-invasion::Stallion Mountain.climax: The emperor praises Xue. Sul gets his lying down.
seventh-invasion::Stallion Mountain.resolution: Namseng takes the flogging. The boy who refused the Tang will one day go over.
seventh-invasion::Stallion Mountain.aPlot: Xue Rengui wants his hour. Sul Gedu wants the cap, the sash and the sword.
seventh-invasion::Stallion Mountain.bPlot: Namseng wants to save his brother.

themes.label: Wrong bones
themes.note: Two outsiders at the same muster.

seventh-invasion::Stallion Mountain.problem: The climax lands at the midpoint, and then three separate endings play out. The capture-and-escape is invented, has no stakes, and reads like filler. The Goguryeo commanders' decision to fight in the open, the real turn of the battle, is never shown.

seventh-invasion::Colossal River.title: Colossal River
seventh-invasion::Colossal River.want: Ulchi Mundeok wants to lure the Sui army to its ruin.
seventh-invasion::Colossal River.development: Beginning: the poem. Middle: a sentence about seven feigned surrenders. End: he gets a title.
seventh-invasion::Colossal River.aPlot: Ulchi Mundeok wants to lure a host to a river.

themes.label: Seven surrenders
themes.note: The best trick in the record, told in a clause.

seventh-invasion::Colossal River.problem: A lore stub. The best trick in Korean military history, walking into the enemy camp and then surrendering seven times, is a single clause, and the river is never shown.

seventh-invasion::Ansi.title: Ansi
seventh-invasion::Ansi.want: The Guardian of Ansi (Yang Manchun) wants to hold the wall for a country whose dictator he defied.
seventh-invasion::Ansi.conflict: The Tang siege mound and the emperor himself.
seventh-invasion::Ansi.development: The unnamed chief · sixty days · the collapse.
seventh-invasion::Ansi.climax: He seizes the slumped mound. An arrow at a helmet.
seventh-invasion::Ansi.resolution: Silk at the foot of the wall. A bow. Crazier than we are.
seventh-invasion::Ansi.aPlot: The Guardian wants to hold the wall for a country whose dictator he defied.
seventh-invasion::Ansi.bPlot: The emperor himself, and a mound that slumps.

themes.label: One person to serve
themes.note: He defied Yeon and still held.

seventh-invasion::Ansi.problem: The mound collapse is a great turn, but the ending is weather, told in summary. The arrow at the helmet is vague, and Yang has no scene with the emperor at the end. The flashback with Gesomun is thin, and so is its later "Madman… he does what must be done."

seventh-invasion::Haemosu.title: Haemosu
seventh-invasion::Haemosu.want: Yuhwa wants the sun god, and on her own terms.
seventh-invasion::Haemosu.development: The chariot stops · the copper room.
seventh-invasion::Haemosu.climax: Exile. The fox leads her to Geumwa.
seventh-invasion::Haemosu.resolution: The egg. He has already gone.
seventh-invasion::Haemosu.aPlot: Yuhwa wants the sun god, on her own terms.
seventh-invasion::Haemosu.bPlot: Habek will not have a sky man in his river.

themes.label: I looked up
themes.note: A god who takes and a river girl who invites.

seventh-invasion::Haemosu.problem: The middle is all desire and no opposition. Habek's court, the real conflict, is three lines. Haemosu then vanishes without any decision being shown.

seventh-invasion::Buyeo.title: Buyeo
seventh-invasion::Buyeo.want: Jumong wants to survive his brother Daeso and get out of Buyeo.
seventh-invasion::Buyeo.conflict: Daeso's knives and nets, and then Haewonmek, the reaper.
seventh-invasion::Buyeo.development: The unbreakable egg · the knife in the dark.
seventh-invasion::Buyeo.climax: The turtle bridge. The three-legged crow.
seventh-invasion::Buyeo.resolution: He crosses. The half sword is still in the north.
seventh-invasion::Buyeo.aPlot: Jumong wants to survive Daeso and get out.
seventh-invasion::Buyeo.bPlot: Haemosu stops a reaper. A horse starved then fattened.

themes.label: Get out
themes.note: A boy the house will not keep.

seventh-invasion::Buyeo.problem: The needle trick, the best plant in the episode, is wasted. Jumong gives the fast horse to Oi and crosses the river on foot. The boyhood section is montage, and Lady Ye is a single beat.

seventh-invasion::Jolbon.title: Jolbon
seventh-invasion::Jolbon.want: Sosuno wants Jumong and won't admit it. Jumong wants a roof of his own.
seventh-invasion::Jolbon.conflict: Her pride, her father Tabal, the well girls, and then the five tribes and Song Yang.
seventh-invasion::Jolbon.development: Tabal’s hall · the bow that will not bend · the well · the grain room.
seventh-invasion::Jolbon.climax: The pine shot. The vermilion cord.
seventh-invasion::Jolbon.resolution: A kingdom from a yard. Everything after is a second episode told as a list.
seventh-invasion::Jolbon.aPlot: Sosuno wants Jumong and will not admit it.
seventh-invasion::Jolbon.bPlot: Jumong wants a roof of his own. The well is where they count.

themes.label: The well
themes.note: She prices a kingdom. He cannot count grain.

seventh-invasion::Jolbon.problem: The romance is complete and climaxes on Tabal's pine shot. Everything after it is a second episode told as a list. Song Yang is beaten with one arrow, and the five tribes unite off-page.

chunchu-era::Gi (起).title: Gi (起)
chunchu-era::Gi (起).want: Bidam wants the throne to go to the cleverest person, not to the last of the Sacred Bone.
chunchu-era::Gi (起).conflict: The unanimous Harmony Council, his brother Yushin, and Alchun's cynicism.
chunchu-era::Gi (起).development: The vote · the lone hand · Biryun at the Class 51 gate · watching Jinji.
chunchu-era::Gi (起).climax: The queen promotes the man who told her council no.
chunchu-era::Gi (起).resolution: He recruits. The word Gaya sits on the table.
chunchu-era::Gi (起).aPlot: Bidam wants the throne to go to the cleverest person, not the last Sacred Bone.
chunchu-era::Gi (起).bPlot: Yumjong says Gaya. A door he pretends not to see.

themes.label: Cleverest, not last
themes.note: The no that crowned her is the no that will unseat her.

chunchu-era::Gi (起).problem: The Yamato cold open belongs to another story. The scene with Princess Seungman has Bidam repeat Chunchu's Gesomun line, which makes no sense coming from him. The real twist, that the queen makes High Councillor the one man who told her council no, is a single narrated sentence.

chunchu-era::Suro.title: Suro
chunchu-era::Suro.want: Suro wants Queen Heo. Before that, Ibiga wants the mountain goddess.
chunchu-era::Suro.conflict: Six eggs on a shore. No country yet.
chunchu-era::Suro.development: Ibiga takes the mountain. The eggs hatch. Six brothers take the hills.
chunchu-era::Suro.climax: Queen Heo arrives from the south.
chunchu-era::Suro.resolution: Gaya has a name, a queen, and a bloodline Bidam will use.
chunchu-era::Suro.aPlot: Suro wants Queen Heo. Before that, Ibiga wants the mountain.
chunchu-era::Suro.bPlot: Six eggs and a Turtle Song.

themes.label: A country that is only a name
themes.note: My country is gone.

chunchu-era::Suro.problem: Two seductions and a fact list, with no obstacle. The Gaya league diagram has no story stake.

chunchu-era::Seung (承).title: Seung (承)
chunchu-era::Seung (承).want: Bidam wants Yushin, and the country, to admit his ideas are right. Chunchu wants a weakness he can exploit.
chunchu-era::Seung (承).conflict: Yushin across the tea table, Alchun's neutrality, and the conscience water.
chunchu-era::Seung (承).development: The cut Maitreya · nightly tea · Jade Gate flashback.
chunchu-era::Seung (承).climax: Have you ever considered the POSSIBILITY that your ideas are simply terrible?
chunchu-era::Seung (承).resolution: The splash is empty. The rant is the turn.
chunchu-era::Seung (承).aPlot: Bidam wants Yushin, and the country, to admit his ideas are right.
chunchu-era::Seung (承).bPlot: Chunchu wants a weakness. The conscience water shows nothing.

themes.label: The real Sillans
themes.note: Yushin keeps him talking on purpose.

chunchu-era::Seung (承).problem: Day 3 is summary, and Alchun's two speeches are position papers read aloud. It's never explained how Chunchu stands at the edge of a pavilion between enemy camps.

chunchu-era::Muryuk.title: Muryuk
chunchu-era::Muryuk.want: Muryuk wants to prove he is Silla, so his sons will not have to.
chunchu-era::Muryuk.conflict: Gaya surrenders. Guhae and his sons take up new jobs in Silla.
chunchu-era::Muryuk.development: Muryuk rises as a Silla general. He meets Sadaham, a young hwarang who inspires new hope and makes him want a son.
chunchu-era::Muryuk.climax: He names himself. He says Dodo. He does not look away.
chunchu-era::Muryuk.resolution: His grandson will not have to prove it.
chunchu-era::Muryuk.aPlot: Muryuk wants to prove he is Silla, so his sons will not have to.
chunchu-era::Muryuk.bPlot: The cone that still says Gaya.

themes.label: Assimilation
themes.note: He does the dying so the sons can be from here.

chunchu-era::Muryuk.problem: The surrender half is still long for a payoff episode. The Gwansan night now does the job the audit asked for.

chunchu-era::Jeon (轉).title: Jeon (轉)
chunchu-era::Jeon (轉).want: Yushin wants to defeat Bidam without losing himself.
chunchu-era::Jeon (轉).conflict: Bidam's "Gaya wretch", the star omen, and the grain running out.
chunchu-era::Jeon (轉).development: The empty sixth night · the headband · Bidam expelled · the cavern.
chunchu-era::Jeon (轉).climax: He kills the horse that saved him. Because it is ours.
chunchu-era::Jeon (轉).resolution: The score breaks. The beads go on a bridle.
chunchu-era::Jeon (轉).aPlot: Yushin wants to defeat Bidam without losing himself.
chunchu-era::Jeon (轉).bPlot: Hangyul. The kite needs a life.

themes.label: Duty
themes.note: Choosing Silla with his own hands.

chunchu-era::Jeon (轉).problem: Yushin's identity crisis is resolved by his dead father and grandfather giving a pep talk in the steam. That's an outside fix, and it comes before his real act. Bidam's beast expulsion is spectacle that touches neither his arc nor the plot.

chunchu-era::Seohyun.title: Seohyun
chunchu-era::Seohyun.want: Seohyeon wants Manmyung, and the Gaya stain wants to be forgiven.
chunchu-era::Seohyun.conflict: Her father locks the door. Heaven has already picked the house.
chunchu-era::Seohyun.development: The horse keeps getting lost. She spends three days looking at a drain.
chunchu-era::Seohyun.climax: Lightning takes the door. She crawls out in good silk.
chunchu-era::Seohyun.resolution: They ride to Manno. The second generation will not have to ask.
chunchu-era::Seohyun.aPlot: Seohyeon wants Manmyung. The Gaya stain wants to be forgiven.

themes.label: Second-generation assimilation
themes.note: Muryuk did the dying. Seohyun does the living.

chunchu-era::Seohyun.problem: The best-built episode in either file, but it runs three codas past the climax (the spring, age fifteen, Daeyang). It also sits between Day 9 and Day 10 and stalls the rebellion's climax.

chunchu-era::Gyul (結).title: Gyul (結)
chunchu-era::Gyul (結).want: Bidam wants to finish the score. Yushin wants it over.
chunchu-era::Gyul (結).conflict: Each other, then Alchun over the purge.
chunchu-era::Gyul (結).development: The last morning · the yard · the count.
chunchu-era::Gyul (結).climax: The head on the packed earth where they first met.
chunchu-era::Gyul (結).resolution: 108–108 is over. Yushin mounts. The order stands.
chunchu-era::Gyul (結).aPlot: The rebellion ends. A head comes back to the dirt.
chunchu-era::Gyul (結).bPlot: Alchun goes pale. Blood is inevitable.

themes.label: Because it is ours
themes.note: The yard keeps the score until it is blood.

chunchu-era::Gyul (結).problem: The closing "twist" twists nothing. It repeats the headband meeting from ep 44, and "it is not the way he has been telling it" sets up a reveal that never comes.

chunchu-era::Queen Jinduk.title: Queen Jinduk
chunchu-era::Queen Jinduk.want: Jinduk wants not to be compared with her cousin.
chunchu-era::Queen Jinduk.development: Beginning: the crown is padded. Middle: the maids whisper. End: Chunchu's moon line and the loom.
chunchu-era::Queen Jinduk.aPlot: A sister takes a throne that was never meant to last.

themes.label: The second queen
themes.note: A fragment between Bidam and the embassy.

chunchu-era::Queen Jinduk.problem: A grace note with no turn. Her one victory, the Tang ode she weaves, is flash-forwarded in a sentence.

chunchu-era::Huangdi (皇帝).title: Huangdi (皇帝)
chunchu-era::Huangdi (皇帝).conflict: The emperor's terms and his court. Later, Wu, and a Goguryeo patrol.
chunchu-era::Huangdi (皇帝).development: The embassy · the hall · the three choices answered.
chunchu-era::Huangdi (皇帝).climax: The emperor agrees. The price is Silla’s pride.
chunchu-era::Huangdi (皇帝).resolution: A war is bought. The man who bought it will not live to spend it all.
chunchu-era::Huangdi (皇帝).aPlot: Chunchu goes to Chang’an to buy a war with a country that does not need him.
chunchu-era::Huangdi (皇帝).bPlot: Wu at the screen. Taizong mispronounces a name.

themes.label: Buying a war
themes.note: The east star, spent in a foreign hall.

chunchu-era::Huangdi (皇帝).problem: The want is granted by a quote in the first act. The real climax, the dying emperor's promise at Saluzi's panel, is followed by five more endings. The Gija/Wiman flashback is a lore dump, and On Gunhae's sacrifice, the episode's true cost, is narrated by a man the reader has never met.

chunchu-era::Jiabeng (駕崩).title: Jiabeng (駕崩)
chunchu-era::Jiabeng (駕崩).want: Gaozong wants to grieve before he has to rule. Wu wants back in.
chunchu-era::Jiabeng (駕崩).development: Beginning: the deathbed. Middle: the temple name, mourning rules, the Turks' petition to die. End: Chunchu reads the will, Wu at Ganye Temple.
chunchu-era::Jiabeng (駕崩).aPlot: An emperor dies. The room changes owners.

themes.label: The death of an emperor
themes.note: A hinge, not a story.

chunchu-era::Jiabeng (駕崩).problem: A procession of events. The two real choices (Gaozong refusing the generals' suicide, Wu holding his gaze) get two lines each, and the Euija and Gyebek lines dangle.

chunchu-era::Royal Secretariat.title: Royal Secretariat
chunchu-era::Royal Secretariat.want: Chunchu wants a brush that moves a country at Tang speed.
chunchu-era::Royal Secretariat.conflict: The Harmony Council, which never appears on the page as a person.
chunchu-era::Royal Secretariat.development: Beginning: the circling petition. Middle: Jukji is named Premier and Tang dress arrives. End: Yamato turns away the robed envoys.
chunchu-era::Royal Secretariat.aPlot: The new hall learns who writes the country.
chunchu-era::Royal Secretariat.bPlot: A chorus of clerks, and a man who will not sit.

themes.label: Who writes the country
themes.note: Too many mouths. Not enough want.

chunchu-era::Royal Secretariat.problem: A list of reforms with no one pushing back. It's also out of order: it's dated 651 but placed before ep 50 (649).

chunchu-era::King Muyeol.title: King Muyeol
chunchu-era::King Muyeol.want: Chunchu wants the throne without seeming to want it.
chunchu-era::King Muyeol.conflict: The unanimity rule and Yushin's doubt.
chunchu-era::King Muyeol.development: Beginning: Jinduk's death and Kangrim. Middle: a holdout is laughed down off-page. End: the coronation and Yushin's "private grudge" challenge.
chunchu-era::King Muyeol.aPlot: Chunchu takes the name the east star promised.

themes.label: The name
themes.note: The vow, finally worn.

chunchu-era::King Muyeol.problem: The holdout, the whole drama of a unanimous council, is summarized. Yushin's challenge about the dead daughter has no setup in this arc.

chunchu-era::Jahee.title: Jahee
chunchu-era::Jahee.want: Bupmin wants to get the sums right, and then Jahee.
chunchu-era::Jahee.development: Beginning: "Your sums are wrong." Middle: a kiss in the rain. End: a two-queens montage and "king for all".
chunchu-era::Jahee.aPlot: Ocean-trade sums on an eastern quay.

themes.label: The harbour marriage
themes.note: Ledgers, then a wife.

chunchu-era::Jahee.problem: A vignette. The only stake is a ledger, and the second half is a time-skip.

chunchu-era::Hyukgosé.title: Hyukgosé
chunchu-era::Hyukgosé.want: The six chiefs want a king.
chunchu-era::Hyukgosé.development: Beginning: the kneeling winged horse. Middle: the egg and Alyoung from the chicken-dragon's rib. End: the founding speech and the five-part body.
chunchu-era::Hyukgosé.aPlot: An egg, a horse, six chiefs. The country invents itself.

themes.label: Founding myth
themes.note: Ink for the egg. Heewon for the crowning.

chunchu-era::Hyukgosé.problem: The horse scene is lovely, but nothing opposes anyone, and the "New Unity" speech is a manifesto.

chunchu-era::Talhae.title: Talhae
chunchu-era::Talhae.want: Talhae wants a house, then a country — and the fire that makes both hold.
chunchu-era::Talhae.conflict: Suro already has the throne; Hogong lives on the best ground; Nuri has more teeth.
chunchu-era::Talhae.development: Beginning: the chest, seven silent days, a season in Gaya’s forges, the challenge with Heo watching. Middle: Toham, the whetstone as Gaya iron, marriage to Ahyo. End: Nuri names him, the elders vote, the yards of Surabol smell of charcoal.
chunchu-era::Talhae.climax: The first vote of the six houses.
chunchu-era::Talhae.resolution: Talhae bows to the floor that lent him the crown, and lights the forges.
chunchu-era::Talhae.aPlot: A boy from a box learns Gaya’s fire, talks his way to a stolen house, then a throne.
chunchu-era::Talhae.bPlot: Nuri wins the rice cake and spends thirty years being kind enough to give it back.

themes.label: The man from the sea
themes.note: Suro’s missing climax, told here.

themes.label: Gaya’s fire
themes.note: He loses the chair and takes the forges north.

chunchu-era::Alji.title: Alji
chunchu-era::Alji.want: Talhae wants to know what heaven is sending him.
chunchu-era::Alji.conflict: None. Heaven's heir comes in a box to a man with sons.
chunchu-era::Alji.development: Beginning: the rooster at night. Middle: the gold box. End: Alji is raised, and the Kims wait seven generations.
chunchu-era::Alji.aPlot: A gold box in a wood. A cock that will not stop.

themes.label: The box in Sirim
themes.note: Ink in the wood. Heewon at court.

chunchu-era::Alji.problem: A charming anecdote with no choice in it.

fall-of-euija::Exile.title: Exile
fall-of-euija::Exile.want: Shared between the Satek elders (they want Gyebek gone before the mourning ends) and Gyebek (he wants to stay at the king's side). Nobody owns the episode.
fall-of-euija::Exile.conflict: Two feuding clans unite against the one man they can't buy. Euija is benched by the mourning rite.
fall-of-euija::Exile.development: B: Gomanari's legend, then the clan truce. M: the name offer, the arrow, Seongchung's warning. E: the seal is read out, Gyebek is shipped off, wakes on a beach, Euija rages, training on the island.
fall-of-euija::Exile.aPlot: Pung is sent away. A prince learns what a story costs.

themes.label: Exile
themes.note: The price of the theatre.

fall-of-euija::Exile.problem: The exile is told three times: "They put him on a ship", "The order comes down… put on a boat", and the hall reading. The Satek-water/Yunbi-contract line also appears twice, so the climax is spent before it arrives. The footprints behind the monastery screen are planted and never paid off, and "Nine, by then" floats with nothing to attach to.

fall-of-euija::Heaven–Earth King.title: Heaven–Earth King
fall-of-euija::Heaven–Earth King.want: It passes through three hands: Chongmyeong (feed her guest), the King (the son from his dream), then Daebyeol (an honest contest). The frame want is Yuri Dora getting Gyebek to sit down.
fall-of-euija::Heaven–Earth King.conflict: Sumyung Jangja's sanded rice, then Sobyeol's swapped flower.
fall-of-euija::Heaven–Earth King.development: B: two suns, the dream, the poor house. M: the sand, Jangja swallowed by the earth, the vine, the comb, the suns shot down. E: the riddles, the flower swap, Daebyeol goes down, Gyebek sits.
fall-of-euija::Heaven–Earth King.aPlot: The sky splits. Two suns. A grandfather telling a tale he was present for.

themes.label: Myth
themes.note: Joseon ink, on purpose.

fall-of-euija::Heaven–Earth King.problem: It runs long, and the Jangja punishment is a complete story nested inside it. Chongmyeong's "I'll be here. I'll have rice on" is the most loaded line in the tale and nothing comes back to it.

fall-of-euija::Sulmun.title: Sulmun
fall-of-euija::Sulmun.want: Sulmun wants to build a bridge to the mainland. Gyebek wants to catch the story out.
fall-of-euija::Sulmun.conflict: Barely any. The famine, then the islanders coming up one roll of silk short.
fall-of-euija::Sulmun.development: B: the giant woman, the apron. M: the porridge death (a separate tale). E: ninety-nine rolls, no bridge.
fall-of-euija::Sulmun.aPlot: A giantess and a mountain that will not stay put.

themes.label: Island myth
themes.note: Tamla’s grandmother.

fall-of-euija::Sulmun.problem: Three micro-myths in a row with no turn. The porridge death and the bridge are unrelated, and the "one per cent" aside explains the joke.

fall-of-euija::Three Princes.title: Three Princes
fall-of-euija::Three Princes.want: Nobody in the princes' section. The real one is the iron-chest son, who wants to come home.
fall-of-euija::Three Princes.conflict: In the main tale, none ("Marriage. Debate later."). In the subplot, parents who cast out their own son.
fall-of-euija::Three Princes.development: B: a diagram and the hole in the ground. M: arrows, a box, a lesson on kindness from the haenyeo. E: the ox divorce, the chest, the son comes home.
fall-of-euija::Three Princes.aPlot: Three boys, one well, a country that is an island.

themes.label: Tamla founding
themes.note: A well as a womb.

fall-of-euija::Three Princes.problem: The title tale is a summary with no conflict. The episode's real story, the exiled son who comes back as the god his family must bow to, is buried in the last third. And it's the story that mirrors Gyebek.

fall-of-euija::Stone Lady.title: Stone Lady
fall-of-euija::Stone Lady.want: Four unrelated tales: a teaser for Kangrim, the Gimnyeong serpent, Sanbangdeok, and Gameunjang.
fall-of-euija::Stone Lady.conflict: In each, an official or a parent wants the wrong thing.
fall-of-euija::Stone Lady.development: B: "Not a kind one". M: a serpent told in one sentence, the stone lady in three. E: Gameunjang, and the rope tested eleven times.
fall-of-euija::Stone Lady.aPlot: A woman waiting turns to stone.

themes.label: Waiting as a fate
themes.note: The island’s other grandmother.

fall-of-euija::Stone Lady.problem: It's an anthology. The serpent and the stone lady are summaries, and the Kangrim teaser repeats the setup that 62 opens with anyway. Gameunjang is the strong tale here: thrown out for telling the truth, while the people who threw her out go blind. That is Gyebek's case and Euija's future, and it gets the least room.

fall-of-euija::Gardener.title: Gardener
fall-of-euija::Gardener.want: Hallakgungi wants his father and then justice for his mother. Jacheongbi wants her scholar alive.
fall-of-euija::Gardener.conflict: The rich man, then heaven's ban on her marriage.
fall-of-euija::Gardener.development: B: Sara Doryeong is called west, the wife waits. M: fifteen years of saying no, the son flees, the mother is murdered. E: the flowers, revenge, resurrection "in order". The Jacheongbi coda follows.
fall-of-euija::Gardener.aPlot: A man who tends what the gods left.

themes.label: Tending
themes.note: Small, finished, enough.

fall-of-euija::Gardener.problem: Hallakgungi is a complete tale. Jacheongbi's tragedy ("They killed him for it") happens off-page, and her flower-field scene has the speaker "sara" saying "Father retired", which muddles who keeps the gate. Gyebek's "Can the dead be fetched back" is the most important plant in the arc (his family, 70) and it gets two lines.

fall-of-euija::Jachungbi.title: Jachungbi
fall-of-euija::Jachungbi.want: Jachungbi wants the boy from the sky, then wants him back from the dead.
fall-of-euija::Jachungbi.conflict: Heaven, which kills him for sitting beside her.
fall-of-euija::Jachungbi.development: Beginning: she cuts her hair to share a desk. Middle: three years, and he hasn't noticed. End: she walks west to fetch him.
fall-of-euija::Jachungbi.aPlot: A goddess who will not be a wife the way the story wants.

themes.label: Refusal
themes.note: Tamla’s own terms.

fall-of-euija::Jachungbi.problem: Short. The walk is almost a sentence.

fall-of-euija::Kangrim.title: Kangrim
fall-of-euija::Kangrim.want: Kangrim wants to close the magistrate's case and get home to his wife.
fall-of-euija::Kangrim.conflict: The magistrate and Yumla both claim him, and they split him in two.
fall-of-euija::Kangrim.development: B: the whole murder case in one paragraph. M: the underworld road, Yumla. E: the split, the crow, Dongbangsak, the ledger rule.
fall-of-euija::Kangrim.aPlot: The psychopomp reads a name and asks the only question he is licensed to ask.

themes.label: Were you X, or Y?
themes.note: His ritual. Do not vary it.

fall-of-euija::Kangrim.problem: The setup (three brothers, flowers, beads, sons, petitions) is a crammed summary. The crow and Dongbangsak are listed as epilogue items, so the origin of the psychopomp has no single climax. His wife feeds the gods and then disappears.

fall-of-euija::Tribute.title: Tribute
fall-of-euija::Tribute.conflict: Baekje against an island that forgot to send oranges, resolved in one sentence.
fall-of-euija::Tribute.development: B: the forgetting. M: the army waits at the harbour. E: the apology.
fall-of-euija::Tribute.aPlot: What a country sends when it cannot send men.

themes.label: Tribute
themes.note: A ledger, not a turn.

fall-of-euija::Tribute.problem: Four paragraphs of exposition whose only job is to explain why the island takes exiles.

fall-of-euija::Coup.title: Coup
fall-of-euija::Coup.want: Euija wants to break the eight clans.
fall-of-euija::Coup.development: B: the martial-law speech. M: the Enabling Law, the sleeves go up, forty-one sons, Chunbok revealed as the spy. E: Chunbok made Premier, the court maid, the Chunbok–Gaozong flash-forward.
fall-of-euija::Coup.aPlot: The room changes owners again. This time from the inside.

themes.label: From the inside
themes.note: A door the narrator has watched before.

fall-of-euija::Coup.problem: Euija never mentions Gyebek once he has power. In 56 he swore to overturn the clans because "you put my man on a boat," and in 65 he answers "That… who?", so the strongest motive of the arc goes missing. The clans' counter-rally is narrated in summary, and the Chunbok–Gaozong scene, five years early, breaks the timeline without setting anything up.

fall-of-euija::Descent.title: Descent
fall-of-euija::Descent.want: Euija (he wants to stop the counting in his dreams) and then Seongchung (he wants open court before the tide).
fall-of-euija::Descent.conflict: The king's wine, and his anger.
fall-of-euija::Descent.development: B: nightmares, Heungsu sent away. M: about a dozen paragraphs of harem montage. E: Seongchung is jailed, starves, Kangrim comes, the letter.
fall-of-euija::Descent.aPlot: Gods come down. The three realms remember they are family.

themes.label: Descent
themes.note: Hannim’s gossip, not scripture.

fall-of-euija::Descent.problem: The middle is a shot list ("They hike the silk. One knee up. A twist."), the exact narration your own style rule bans, repeated at least eight times with no escalation. Seongchung, the real protagonist, arrives in the last fifth and gets one attempt.

fall-of-euija::Nine Omens.title: Nine Omens
fall-of-euija::Nine Omens.want: Euija wants a reading the sky can still give him.
fall-of-euija::Nine Omens.conflict: Chunchu's manufactured omens, and Euija's own past as a maker of miracles.
fall-of-euija::Nine Omens.resolution: Sabi already knows. The court will pretend it does not.
fall-of-euija::Nine Omens.aPlot: The country answers before the army does.
fall-of-euija::Nine Omens.bPlot: Toads in the pines. A guard with a lantern.

themes.label: The country knows first
themes.note: Weather as plot.

fall-of-euija::Nine Omens.problem: The numbered list is a lore dump. Every omen is reported, and Euija sees none of them until the turtle. The irony (the man who invented the white deer, undone by fake omens) is stated in narration instead of being discovered by Euija.

fall-of-euija::Onjo.title: Onjo
fall-of-euija::Onjo.want: Yuri (find his father), then Sosuno (not to be a footnote), then Onjo (a kingdom).
fall-of-euija::Onjo.conflict: Yuri's arrival pushes Sosuno's sons out of the succession. Biryu wants the sea.
fall-of-euija::Onjo.development: B: Yuri's half-sword (a summary). M: the last night at the well and in the grain room. E: the white stag, Mount Buak, Biryu splits off, the name "Baekje".
fall-of-euija::Onjo.aPlot: A second son wants a country that is not his brother’s.
fall-of-euija::Onjo.bPlot: Wirye. The south. A house from nothing.

themes.label: The second house
themes.note: Baekje begins as a refusal.

fall-of-euija::Onjo.problem: Placement kills it. It lands right after "Summon Gyebek…!", the arc's biggest cliffhanger, and stalls the countdown for a story from 18 BC. Onjo is passive (the deer decides for him), and the real climax, "Who's Mother coming with?", is left unanswered.

fall-of-euija::Sunchung.title: Sunchung
fall-of-euija::Sunchung.want: Sunchung wants the king to hear one word before he dies: hold Chimhyun and Final Ford.
fall-of-euija::Sunchung.conflict: The feast on the other side of the wall, and a wine jar on the paper.
fall-of-euija::Sunchung.development: B: the last lamp with Hungsu (Chimhyun / Final Ford split). M: the cell, one sheet, the footsteps that come back empty. E: four years later Euija finds the paper, names Hungsu, and a courier rides for Gomamiji. Ye Sikjin does his sums in the back of the hall.
fall-of-euija::Sunchung.resolution: The ask is the plant. 660 will pay it with an empty pass.
fall-of-euija::Sunchung.aPlot: Sunchung wants the pass held. He is in prison.
fall-of-euija::Sunchung.bPlot: Euija will not listen. The door is already open.

themes.label: The man in prison
themes.note: The last honest ask.

fall-of-euija::Sunchung.problem: The 660 market / Eraha frame is still Euija's, so Sunchung's want is carried in flashback. The dying memorial is read aloud in the letter scene (the widgets already hold the Sagi text).

fall-of-euija::Hungsu.title: Hungsu
fall-of-euija::Hungsu.want: Hungsu wants to be asked, and to be used.
fall-of-euija::Hungsu.conflict: Distance, the ministers' contempt, and time.
fall-of-euija::Hungsu.development: B: the map in the dirt. M: the courier, same paper as Sunchung. E: Sabi — Euija holds both papers, "So it is", the sleeve; eleven mornings of no second letter; rain; walking north.
fall-of-euija::Hungsu.aPlot: A man who already lost tries to save what is left.

themes.label: Too late
themes.note: The other warning.

fall-of-euija::Hungsu.problem: The berth flashback is dated 655. The Yusa "chickens in a basket" quote still injects beside the dramatized Sabi scene.

fall-of-euija::Gyebek.title: Gyebek
fall-of-euija::Gyebek.want: Gyebek wants to keep his promise.
fall-of-euija::Gyebek.conflict: Yuri Dora's "a story is not begun with its ending fixed", and his own family.
fall-of-euija::Gyebek.development: The house · the road to Hwangsan.
fall-of-euija::Gyebek.climax: The reverse grip. The last line.
fall-of-euija::Gyebek.resolution: Kangrim will ask. The word is finally spent.
fall-of-euija::Gyebek.aPlot: Gyebek wants five thousand to mean something.
fall-of-euija::Gyebek.bPlot: He kills his family first so nothing can be used against him.

themes.label: Nothing to use against him
themes.note: The captain who holds his sword backwards.

fall-of-euija::Gyebek.problem: The defining act, killing his wife and children, happens off-page. Worse, the family has never appeared in the serial, so 72's quote about "my wife and children" has nothing behind it. The farewell's "My lord… I am a man with no name" repeats itself.

epilogue-part-ii::Three Realms.title: Three Realms
epilogue-part-ii::Three Realms.want: Arguably Kangrim, who wants to know whether a dead person can be brought back.
epilogue-part-ii::Three Realms.conflict: Sara's suspicion, and the gods' rule against interfering.
epilogue-part-ii::Three Realms.development: B: servants gossiping, the Samsin/Haemosu flirtation. M: the reunification line. E: Kangrim's question, and "Let the meeting begin."
epilogue-part-ii::Three Realms.climax: Haemosu flirtation. M: the reunification line. E: Kangrim's question, and "Let the meeting begin."
epilogue-part-ii::Three Realms.aPlot: Living, Dead, and the Western Flower Field keep house.

themes.label: 삼계
themes.note: A map of heaven, not a plot.

epilogue-part-ii::Three Realms.problem: A party with no turn, and the meeting it builds up to never happens ("The minutes never leave"). The Samsin/Haemosu flirtation is half the length with no stakes. "Hallakgungi alone" enters, but the speaker is `sara`, so it's unclear whether this is the Gardener or his father.

fall-of-baekje::Yellow Mountain.title: Yellow Mountain
fall-of-baekje::Yellow Mountain.want: Gyebek wants to hold the door to Sabi.
fall-of-baekje::Yellow Mountain.conflict: Yushin and fifty thousand men, plus Su Dingfang's deadline.
fall-of-baekje::Yellow Mountain.development: The last line · the boys · the disputed blade.
fall-of-baekje::Yellow Mountain.climax: The field is taken. The reverse grip ends.
fall-of-baekje::Yellow Mountain.resolution: Kangrim’s question. Hwangsan is the grave of a word.
fall-of-baekje::Yellow Mountain.aPlot: Gyebek meets fifty thousand with five thousand.
fall-of-baekje::Yellow Mountain.bPlot: Yushin wants the field. Gwanchang wants a name.

themes.label: Five thousand
themes.note: A man measured by self-control, spent.

fall-of-baekje::Yellow Mountain.problem: The "Yellow Mountain Fields" paragraph spoils the duel ("Blue plume cuts yellow lacquer") as a prompt fragment. Kangrim asks his question twice, and the second exchange is Gyebek reciting episode 62 back to him. Gyebek's death is off-page ("finishes counting, and walks").

fall-of-baekje::Sabi.title: Sabi
fall-of-baekje::Sabi.want: Euija wants to survive with something left to bargain with.
fall-of-baekje::Sabi.conflict: Su Dingfang, Silla, and the doors opened from the inside (his son, his grandson, Ye Sikjin).
fall-of-baekje::Sabi.development: B: the refused feast. M: Yushin's axe, the flight, the prince spat on, Falling Flower Rock, Ye Sikjin. E: Chunchu's cup, the pagoda, the commanderies, "the dog bites".
fall-of-baekje::Sabi.aPlot: The capital falls. Euija wants one more story.
fall-of-baekje::Sabi.bPlot: The ford was empty. Sunchung was right.

themes.label: The last story
themes.note: A country is a territory governed by a single story.

fall-of-baekje::Sabi.problem: Too many beats, with three protagonists (Yushin, Euija, Chunchu). The "KIM CHUNCHU!!!" shout is reused word for word in 74. Gumil's execution, the payoff to Daeya, gets one clause. The Falling Flower Rock and the court maids are split across two places.

fall-of-baekje::Buyeo Euija†.title: Buyeo Euija†
fall-of-baekje::Buyeo Euija†.want: Euija wants to write his own ending.
fall-of-baekje::Buyeo Euija†.conflict: The Tang confession, which is his story written by someone else.
fall-of-baekje::Buyeo Euija†.development: B: the confession comedy. M: Su Dingfang's praise of Silla, the shout. E: Kangrim, then a long obituary essay.
fall-of-baekje::Buyeo Euija†.aPlot: Kangrim reads the name. Were you a king, or a storyteller?

themes.label: The question
themes.note: His ritual.

fall-of-baekje::Buyeo Euija†.problem: The confession is the best scene in the arc, then the eulogy explains what we just watched ("He was right about everything… He falls because he arranged…"), which breaks your no-decoder rule. Haewonmek and Kangrim both run his exit.

fall-of-baekje::Kim Chunchu†.title: Kim Chunchu†
fall-of-baekje::Kim Chunchu†.want: Chunchu wants to know he has paid, and to hand Bupmin the right dream.
fall-of-baekje::Kim Chunchu†.conflict: Almost none. There's only the risk that Bupmin inherits revenge instead of the dream.
fall-of-baekje::Kim Chunchu†.development: B: temple, fever. M: "Have I paid?", Gotaso, "a king for all". E: the promise, Kangrim, an obituary.
fall-of-baekje::Kim Chunchu†.aPlot: Kangrim reads the name. Were you a king, or a man who bought a war?

themes.label: The question
themes.note: The east star, put down for good.

fall-of-baekje::Kim Chunchu†.problem: A deathbed blessing with nobody pushing back. Yushin, the other half of the "hill" promise, is missing, and the obituary again decodes the life.

fall-of-baekje::Ungjin Commandery.title: Ungjin Commandery
fall-of-baekje::Ungjin Commandery.want: Split: Liu Rengui (earn his office back), Munmu (dignity), Gaozong (his father's war).
fall-of-baekje::Ungjin Commandery.development: B: the net of commanderies. M: Liu's calendar, the Gyerim edict. E: the Four Beasts, an edict quote.
fall-of-baekje::Ungjin Commandery.aPlot: The Tang rename a country and call it administration.

themes.label: A commandery
themes.note: The story is being rewritten from the west.

fall-of-baekje::Ungjin Commandery.problem: A setup episode with no climax. Two diagrams in a row, and it ends on a quoted edict. The strongest seed, Daeto admiring the Tang calendar, is a throwaway.

fall-of-baekje::King Pungjang.title: King Pungjang
fall-of-baekje::King Pungjang.want: Pung wants to be a king, not just a name.
fall-of-baekje::King Pungjang.conflict: Boksin, who holds the army, and Liu Rengui.
fall-of-baekje::King Pungjang.development: B: Seven-Branched Sword flashback, the Asuka court. M: the roll-call comedy, the Jomi-gon flashback, Boksin's needle. E: the Pisong move, summarized, then the debate.
fall-of-baekje::King Pungjang.aPlot: The exiled son comes back with Yamato ships.
fall-of-baekje::King Pungjang.bPlot: A restoration that is already late.

themes.label: The returned son
themes.note: Theatre, with other people’s boats.

fall-of-baekje::King Pungjang.problem: Three flashbacks interrupt it. The Jomi-gon/Imja plant goes unpaid here. The Pisong episode narrates its outcome ("forced to move back") before the debate, and the debate is two annal speeches read aloud.

final-stand::Pyongyang I.title: Pyongyang I
final-stand::Pyongyang I.want: Nobody holds the whole episode. The Red Fowl (Su Dingfang) wants Pyongyang, Namseng wants to hold the river, and Yushin steps up at the very end.
final-stand::Pyongyang I.conflict: Winter, Goguryeo, and the Tang emperor's caution.
final-stand::Pyongyang I.development: Beginning: Gaozong and Wu Zetian argue at court. Middle: the river freezes and Namseng is routed in summary. End: Yushin volunteers to carry the rice.
final-stand::Pyongyang I.aPlot: The first try at the northern capital.

themes.label: Not yet
themes.note: A wall that still holds.

final-stand::Pyongyang I.problem: This is a montage of three camps, and its one turn (the ice) gets two sentences. The payoff of Yushin's offer happens in the next episode.

final-stand::Snake River.title: Snake River
final-stand::Snake River.want: Gesomun wants to destroy the White Tiger (Pang Xiaotai) and his whole line.
final-stand::Snake River.conflict: Pang Xiaotai and his thirteen sons, then the reapers Kangrim and Haewonmek.
final-stand::Snake River.development: Beginning: the counting massacre. Middle: Pang Xiaotai dies, Xue Rengui inherits his title. End: the reapers are defied, then the rice road.
final-stand::Snake River.aPlot: A river that will not stay a border.

themes.label: The snake
themes.note: Water as a plot.

final-stand::Snake River.problem: The best set piece in the arc comes first, and everything after it is anticlimax. The reaper scene ("arrows spent, horse down") happens after Gesomun has already won, so his near-death has no stakes. Xue and the rice road are two more episodes' worth of material.

final-stand::Tamla Surrenders.title: Tamla Surrenders
final-stand::Tamla Surrenders.development: Three lines of summary plus the next-episode card.
final-stand::Tamla Surrenders.aPlot: The island sends a word instead of an army.

themes.label: Surrender as weather
themes.note: Tamla knows when a story is over.

final-stand::Tamla Surrenders.problem: This is a caption, not an episode.

final-stand::Rebellion.title: Rebellion
final-stand::Rebellion.want: Kim Jinju wants the war to be over for him. Munmu wants to be obeyed in his first year as king.
final-stand::Rebellion.conflict: The king against his own True Bone lords.
final-stand::Rebellion.development: Beginning: Jinju calls in sick. Middle: Naesaji falls without him and Heumsun reports who was missing. End: the beheadings, and Punghun waiting in Chang'an.
final-stand::Rebellion.aPlot: A rising that already has its ending written.

themes.label: Do not announce the failure
themes.note: Show the want. Withhold the fall.

final-stand::Rebellion.problem: The turn (Heumsun's report) is told rather than shown, and the paragraph debating whether there were two Jinjus kills the momentum right after the climax. The title points to a Baekje revolt that never appears on the page.

final-stand::Betrayal.title: Betrayal
final-stand::Betrayal.want: Boksin wants to be the man who really runs the Baekje restoration.
final-stand::Betrayal.conflict: First the monk Dochim, then King Pung.
final-stand::Betrayal.development: Beginning: Dochim's arrogance. Middle: the murder at supper. End: a one-line summary of Boksin's fake-illness plot, then his head in a jar.
final-stand::Betrayal.aPlot: The sad thing about betrayal is that it never comes from your enemies.

themes.label: Betrayal
themes.note: A door opened from the inside.

final-stand::Betrayal.problem: The plant is excellent: "Pung remembers the answer. He has two years to think about it." But the payoff, Boksin feigning sickness to lure Pung, is a single summary sentence, so the real climax happens off the page. The flashback label also covers events up to 663, which muddles the chronology.

final-stand::White River.title: White River
final-stand::White River.want: Split between Liu Rengui (wants to win the river mouth), Buyeo Yung (wants to face his brother), Takutsu (wants Baekje to survive) and Pung (wants a feast and a fleet).
final-stand::White River.conflict: The Yamato–Baekje fleet against the Tang line and the tide.
final-stand::White River.development: Beginning: the four banners and Pung abandoning Juryu. Middle: Liu Rengui's plan, the shore charge, the probe on the 27th. End: the fire on the 28th, Pung's sword, Juryu's surrender, and Sangji turning.
final-stand::White River.aPlot: Four fleets in one mouth. Four hundred eastern ships burn.
final-stand::White River.bPlot: Gyebek’s ford, reused by other men.

themes.label: The first time all four met
themes.note: A river that keeps its name.

final-stand::White River.problem: There are about eleven quote blocks, and many beats are told three times (narration, dialogue, quote), which breaks the "one quote per event" rule. The best through-line, Yung waiting to see his brother's banner, is buried under fleet arithmetic and Munmu's side charge.

final-stand::Yeon Gesomun†.title: Yeon Gesomun†
final-stand::Yeon Gesomun†.want: Gesomun wants to cheat death once more and keep his sons from tearing each other apart.
final-stand::Yeon Gesomun†.conflict: Yumla, the king of the underworld, and his own sons.
final-stand::Yeon Gesomun†.development: Beginning: the deathbed warning. Middle: Yumla himself arrives instead of his clerks. End: Gesomun dies, and a long essay sums up his life.
final-stand::Yeon Gesomun†.aPlot: Kangrim reads the name. Were you a guardian, or a dictator?

themes.label: The question
themes.note: Half, son.

final-stand::Yeon Gesomun†.problem: The Yumla payoff of the Snake River refusal is good. Everything after it is a decoder essay that spoils episode 85 ("Nine months after… his sons were at war… his eldest was riding west").

final-stand::Brothers’ Coup.title: Brothers’ Coup
final-stand::Brothers’ Coup.want: Namseng wants to keep his father's title.
final-stand::Brothers’ Coup.conflict: His brothers Namgun and Namsan, and the whisperers between them.
final-stand::Brothers’ Coup.development: Beginning: Gaozong's edict and the provincial tour. Middle: the captured spy, the gates shut. End: Namseng defects to Gaozong, and Jungto takes twelve cities to Silla.
final-stand::Brothers’ Coup.aPlot: Namseng’s brothers want the house. The boy who took a flogging goes west.

themes.label: The sons
themes.note: The flogging, paid.

final-stand::Brothers’ Coup.problem: The episode opens on an archival edict spoken aloud. The whisperers are never seen. "A messenger… meets him in his quarters" is a beat that just stops. The exchange at the gate is garbled ("Insolent— no. Then what would you have me do?").

final-stand::Pyongyang II.title: Pyongyang II
final-stand::Pyongyang II.conflict: The Tang armies, his brother Namseng, and the monk Shinsung.
final-stand::Pyongyang II.development: Beginning: the siege. Middle: the monk is trusted and the empty alms bowl is planted. End: the gates are opened in summary, Namgun's failed suicide, Bojang at Zhaoling, then Yushin's promotion.
final-stand::Pyongyang II.aPlot: The northern capital falls. The wall Yeon walked is someone else’s.

themes.label: The second try
themes.note: This time the wall does not hold.

final-stand::Pyongyang II.problem: The empty alms bowl is planted well, but the betrayal is a one-sentence summary and Namgun never sees it coming or learns of it. "Goguryeo never dies" is said twice. The Yushin promotion coda gives credit to a man who does nothing in the episode.

silla-tang-war::Dangun & Old Joseon.title: Dangun & Old Joseon
