silla-tang-war::Dangun & Old Joseon.want: First half: the bear-woman Ungnyeo wants to be human, then wants Hwanung. Second half: the defender Seong Gi wants to hold Wanggeom.
silla-tang-war::Dangun & Old Joseon.conflict: The tiger and the hundred days, then Han and the traitors inside the city.
silla-tang-war::Dangun & Old Joseon.development: Beginning: a lore dump with a diagram, a quote and the 360 matters. Middle: the seduction under the birch. End: Joseon falls to "a door opened from the inside."
silla-tang-war::Dangun & Old Joseon.aPlot: A bear, a tiger, a cave. A grandfather naming a country.

themes.label: Joseon
themes.note: The word the book has been withholding.

silla-tang-war::Dangun & Old Joseon.problem: These are two unrelated stories with no shared lead. The actual contest, bear against tiger in the cave, is skipped ("The bear stays"). Dropped into the middle of the Silla–Tang war, it stops the arc's momentum.

silla-tang-war::Prosperity Mountain.title: Prosperity Mountain
silla-tang-war::Prosperity Mountain.want: Munmu wants to keep his father's promised land. Yushin wants to spare his king a humiliation.
silla-tang-war::Prosperity Mountain.conflict: The Tang covenant that makes Munmu swear brotherhood with Buyeo Yung.
silla-tang-war::Prosperity Mountain.development: Beginning: Yung installed at Bear Ford. Middle: the Tang choose Hanseul as the white horse for the oath. End: the stable scene, "Find me a war instead."
silla-tang-war::Prosperity Mountain.aPlot: A field, a vow, a country that is now one story.

themes.label: One country
themes.note: The east star, on a mountain.

silla-tang-war::Prosperity Mountain.problem: It is out of order: set in 665, it sits after 668 at the head of the 670–676 arc. Its next-episode card jumps to Dangun for no reason.

silla-tang-war::Ansung.title: Ansung
silla-tang-war::Ansung.want: Anseung wants to survive and save four thousand households.
silla-tang-war::Ansung.conflict: Geom Mojam, who wants to die on the Taedong.
silla-tang-war::Ansung.development: Beginning: the Tang protectorate. Middle: a single argument. End: the murder (one line) and a seal from Munmu.
silla-tang-war::Ansung.aPlot: A name on a road. A fragment.

themes.label: Fragment
themes.note: Needs a want.

silla-tang-war::Ansung.problem: The only act of violence happens in a summary sentence, and Anseung never has a scene with Munmu, who decides his fate.

silla-tang-war::Letters.title: Letters
silla-tang-war::Letters.want: Munmu wants to tell the empire the truth without apologizing.
silla-tang-war::Letters.conflict: Xue Rengui by letter, and the cautious official Daeto inside his own room.
silla-tang-war::Letters.development: Beginning: Xue's letter arrives with a monk. Middle: the night of dictation and Daeto's secret second letter. End: the curt notes back and forth, and seventy captured transports ("Late. As usual.").
silla-tang-war::Letters.aPlot: Munmu wants the war in writing before it is in blood.

themes.label: The war on paper
themes.note: A king who writes.

silla-tang-war::Letters.problem: Munmu's reply is a five-paragraph monologue that nobody interrupts. Daeto's planted letter pays off off-page, as one line in episode 93.

silla-tang-war::Stone Gate.title: Stone Gate
silla-tang-war::Stone Gate.conflict: The Tang and the Mohe cavalry, in summary.
silla-tang-war::Stone Gate.development: Beginning: the chase. Middle: three sentences of defeat. End: a flashback in which Chunchu lays out his long strategy.
silla-tang-war::Stone Gate.aPlot: A gate. A stand. A list.

themes.label: Fragment
themes.note: A battle without a face.

silla-tang-war::Stone Gate.problem: The battle is told in summary. The flashback is an exposition key (good, but a lecture), and it gives away the plan the next five episodes play out.

silla-tang-war::Wonsul.title: Wonsul
silla-tang-war::Wonsul.want: Wonsul wants his father to take him back.
silla-tang-war::Wonsul.conflict: Yushin's pride in being Gaya-born and having to prove it.
silla-tang-war::Wonsul.development: Beginning: Yushin disowns him. Middle: Yushin asks the king for his son's execution. End: Wonsul works a stranger's fields under no name.
silla-tang-war::Wonsul.aPlot: A son who will not be his father’s duty.

themes.label: The son who refuses
themes.note: Yushin’s house, unfinished.

silla-tang-war::Wonsul.problem: Wonsul hardly speaks before his exile. The narrator explains Yushin's motive ("a house that arrived in Silla by treaty…") instead of letting it come out in a scene.

silla-tang-war::Kim Yushin†.title: Kim Yushin†
silla-tang-war::Kim Yushin†.want: Yushin wants to know whether he was ever let in.
silla-tang-war::Kim Yushin†.development: Beginning: a last visit to the steam cavern. Middle: the deathbed and Kangrim's question. End: Munhee, an obituary essay, Daeto executed in one line, then Lady Jiso refuses Wonsul.
silla-tang-war::Kim Yushin†.aPlot: Kangrim reads the name. Were you a marshal, or a brother?

themes.label: The question
themes.note: He stood.

silla-tang-war::Kim Yushin†.problem: There are four codas after the climax ("I wanted in"), and one of them is a decoder essay that restates the answer he just gave. The cavern scene has no turn. Daeto's execution is wasted.

silla-tang-war::Munmu.title: Munmu
silla-tang-war::Munmu.want: Munmu, the day after Yushin's funeral, needs to decide whether to write the West a real apology (the council's wish, with his brother held in Chang'an as a spare king) or finish the war with no uncle and no father.
silla-tang-war::Munmu.conflict: Deto's treason and the peace party outside; inside the cave, every ancestor refuses to simply answer him. Sunduk asks who in the council has been hungry, Yushin says write it but don't chase, Heo says they already took his name, Suro asks "Whose dead?", and the man in white won't speak plainly.
silla-tang-war::Munmu.development: Deto signs his own warrant · the cave, a trimmed goddess beat, the oracle · Sunduk on the ledge · Yushin returns (Hyullé, "Princess", "Is he eating?") · two hands on his shoulders, then the two lines of ancestors back to the founders · the four founders: names, "Whose dead?", "Who does a king serve?", "someone higher up" · the man in white in rhyme: the door riddle, "Ask your mother", "You know better than I" → "Ask them" · the faces in the water · Suro's mound and the Garak-guk gi edict, the turtle song's last line
silla-tang-war::Munmu.climax: Baekje ranks, the apology signed with the emperor's name, rice to Wonsul, Munhee at the well: "Both."
silla-tang-war::Munmu.aPlot: Bupmin wants the headband to have meant something. Now it is a crown.
silla-tang-war::Munmu.bPlot: The dragon. The east sea. A king who will not stay buried on land.

themes.label: The name that was a headband
themes.note: The Five Precepts, spent.

silla-tang-war::Munmu.problem: Long (about 3,900 words) and dense with cameos. The founders' scene leans on the reader recognising Suro from Gyul.

silla-tang-war::Maeso.title: Maeso
silla-tang-war::Maeso.want: Munhun wants to stop the landing, a Silla commander wants the horses, and Wonsul wants to redeem Seokmun. Xue is the antagonist.
silla-tang-war::Maeso.conflict: Xue's landing, guided by Punghun, and the Mohe army.
silla-tang-war::Maeso.development: Beginning: the ambush on the beach. Middle: the horse-cut at Maeso. End: Xue withdraws, and the count of horses comes in.
silla-tang-war::Maeso.aPlot: A fortress, a last Tang line.

themes.label: The last line
themes.note: Silla-Tang, almost done.

silla-tang-war::Maeso.problem: Punghun has been set up across three episodes and then does nothing on the page. Wonsul's redemption, his refusal of rank, is told in summary, and the Maeso lead is an unnamed "Silla commander."

silla-tang-war::Final Ford.title: Final Ford
silla-tang-war::Final Ford.want: Sideuk wants to end the war at sea.
silla-tang-war::Final Ford.conflict: Xue's big ships, and the tide.
silla-tang-war::Final Ford.development: Beginning: Sideuk is handed the fleet. Middle: two losses. End: the mudflat trick, reported in a quote, then "Have we… won…?"
silla-tang-war::Final Ford.aPlot: The mouth of the Geum. Silla’s victory here ends the western war.
silla-tang-war::Final Ford.bPlot: Sunchung died begging someone to hold it.

themes.label: The ford, paid
themes.note: The prison ask, sixteen years late.

silla-tang-war::Final Ford.problem: The three-tries structure is good, but the winning try is reported through a quote. Xue is missing from his own last battle.

silla-tang-war::Wanggum.title: Wanggum
silla-tang-war::Wanggum.want: Munhee wants her son to hold still, and Munmu wants to be king of all Samhan.
silla-tang-war::Wanggum.development: Beginning: Munhee straightens his collar. Middle: a summary jump to 681 and his sea burial. End: the 692 dispute over the name Taejong.
silla-tang-war::Wanggum.aPlot: A guest in a western capital. The king for all is a title someone else wears.

themes.label: The guest
themes.note: The book’s title, spent as irony.

silla-tang-war::Wanggum.problem: The collar scene is lovely but has no turn, and the sea burial, which could be the climax, is told through a quote.

epilogue-2::Balhae.title: Balhae
epilogue-2::Balhae.want: Gulgul wants to carry the crown fragment north and keep his son alive.
epilogue-2::Balhae.conflict: The cold, and the fear of being seen with gold.
epilogue-2::Balhae.development: Beginning: the march through snow. Middle: the gold is revealed and a flashback shows Gesomun taking in a Mohe boy. End: "Goguryeo never dies," then cut to black.
epilogue-2::Balhae.aPlot: A country rises where another fell. The story is not over.

themes.label: After
themes.note: The next episode card, as a country.

epilogue-2::Balhae.problem: The heading says 698 but the scene is the winter of 668. The opening line ("the cold that Yeon once pulled a Mohe boy out of") spoils the flashback before it arrives.

chunchu-era::Bihyung.title: Bihyung
chunchu-era::Bihyung.want: Surabol's madman — a prince — wants to stay useful after the living have used him.
chunchu-era::Bihyung.conflict: Jinji's fall, the Ghost Children, a court that needs a fool and will not keep one.
chunchu-era::Bihyung.development: The night work · the dressed stones · the servants say goblins.
chunchu-era::Bihyung.climax: By morning the Ghost Bridge is there.
chunchu-era::Bihyung.resolution: The identity box stays shut. Yongsu walks the same stream.
chunchu-era::Bihyung.aPlot: A boy who talks to the dark is asked to put a bridge on a ditch.
chunchu-era::Bihyung.bPlot: Suulbu’s house. Chunmyung’s sums. The fox that built it.

themes.label: The streak
themes.note: Do not open the box.

chunchu-era::Bihyung.problem: A life, like Yongsu. A few nights could be one night.

chunchu-era::Kim Yongsu.title: Kim Yongsu
chunchu-era::Kim Yongsu.want: Yongsu wants the Ghost Children back among the living without putting his cousin off the chair, and without handing his son the story.
chunchu-era::Kim Yongsu.conflict: The Council’s purge-list; Gildal’s last night; a king who will not hear a confession; a queen who will.
chunchu-era::Kim Yongsu.development: The goblins unmasked · rice cakes under the bridge · the madman’s arithmetic.
chunchu-era::Kim Yongsu.climax: Yongsu is forced to kill Gildal, who reassures him.
chunchu-era::Kim Yongsu.resolution: The fox is thrown off its own stones. The house keeps the weather.
chunchu-era::Kim Yongsu.aPlot: Yongsu wants the night to stay useful, and Chunmyung to sit down beside the sums.
chunchu-era::Kim Yongsu.bPlot: Chunchu is nine and learns to say nothing. Suulbu taps each stone.

themes.label: A bridge nobody ordered
themes.note: She married into that weather.

chunchu-era::Kim Yongsu.problem: It is still a life. Chunchu’s shame is told as a verdict before we watch him be ashamed.
